description: Figure 5 is described by its caption as a six-panel composite, but only panel (a) is supplied: engineering stress-strain curves for Fe-10Al-15Mn-0.8C-5Ni wt% low-density steel in HR, CR and 5-30 min annealed conditions. Axes: y = engineering stress, MPa, with gridlines at 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200 and 1500; x = engineering strain, % with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Six labelled curves: CR (red) peaks at or just above the 1500 MPa gridline below 2% strain and then drops steeply; HR (black) peaks between the 900 and 1200 MPa gridlines and terminates near 7% strain; A5 (green), A15 (blue), A10 (dark red) and A30 (cyan) sit progressively lower in stress but extend to roughly 11%, 16%, 15% and 20% strain, A30 being the most ductile and lowest in strength. An inset table headed "Toughness, kJ/mol or (J/cm3)" prints HR: 0.48 (66.5); CR: 0.11 (15.2); A05: 0.64 (90.1); A10: 0.69 (95.8); A15: 0.85 (117.8); A30: 0.89 (123.3). The panel therefore demonstrates a strength-ductility-toughness trade-off: CR maximises strength while destroying ductility, and longer annealing raises ductility and absorbed energy at the cost of strength. Panels (b)-(f) - optical/SEM images and an EBSD phase map - are not present in the supplied image.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots engineering stress (MPa, gridlines 0/300/600/900/1200/1500) against engineering strain (%, ticks 0/5/10/15/20) for six labelled conditions.
The CR curve (red) attains the highest peak, reaching at or just above the 1500 MPa gridline at less than 2% strain, then drops steeply; no fracture strain value is printed for it.
The HR curve (black) peaks between the 900 and 1200 MPa gridlines and terminates at roughly 7% engineering strain.
A30 (cyan) is the most ductile curve, extending to about 20% strain, while A5 (green) ends near 11%, A10 (dark red) near 15% and A15 (blue) near 16% strain.
The same condition is printed two ways in panel (a): the curve is labelled "A5" while the inset toughness table lists "A05".
The caption states panel (a) shows engineering stress-strain curves giving strength-ductility and toughness variations for samples processed under HR, CR and 5-30 min annealing.

The caption states the group also contains optical and SEM images of (b,e) stringer band annihilation, (c) crack formation and (d) microvoid nucleation at the deformed tensile gauge, plus (f) an EBSD phase map revealing grain boundaries inside B2 stringer bands; these panels are not present in the supplied image.
The citing text states the HR condition exhibits nearly 6.8% ductility and that CR reduces it further.
The citing text states the tensile strength in A15 was higher than that of A10, and that ductility in A30 increased slightly despite a longer annealing time.

The citing text states the energy absorbed before fracture, obtained by integrating the area under the stress-strain curves, increases moderately with annealing time of the samples (inset, Figure 5a).
The citing text states that EBSD phase mapping in Figure 5f pinpoints crack initiation at the grain boundaries of B2 stringer bands, which statically recrystallise into a bamboo-like structure.
The citing text states that macrovoids nucleate inside B2 stringer bands and coalesce into crack initiation inside those bands as tensile strain increases (Figure 5d).

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (y = engineering stress, MPa, 0-1500; x = engineering strain, %, 0-20) with six labelled curves: CR (red, highest peak at/above 1500 MPa, fractures below ~2% strain), HR (black, peak between 900 and 1200 MPa, ends near 7%), A5 (green, ~11%), A15 (blue, ~16%), A10 (dark red, ~15%) and A30 (cyan, ~20%, lowest stress). An inset table prints toughness in kJ/mol (J/cm3) for HR, CR, A05, A10, A15 and A30.

Described by the caption as optical and SEM images (b,e: stringer band annihilation; c: crack formation; d: microvoid nucleation at the deformed tensile gauge) and an EBSD phase map (f) revealing grain boundaries inside B2 stringer bands. These panels were not supplied and nothing about them can be visually confirmed.
